subject: math
title: Numerical Expressions and the Order of Operations
seo_title: Grade 5 Numerical Expressions Worksheets: Order of Operations with Parentheses, Brackets and Braces
standard_text: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols. Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them. For example, express the calculation “add 8 and 7, then multiply by 2” as 2 × (8 + 7). Recognize that 3 × (18,932 + 921) is three times as large as 18,932 + 921, without having to calculate the indicated sum or product.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 numerical expressions worksheets: evaluate expressions with parentheses, brackets and braces, use the order of operations, write expressions from words, and compare expressions without calculating. 100 practice questions with step-by-step answers.
key_big: Grouping symbols first, from the inside out. Then × and ÷, then + and −, each from left to right.
key_sub: 5 + 3 × 4 = 5 + 12 = 17, not 32. 24 ÷ 4 × 2 = 6 × 2 = 12. 3 × (18,932 + 921) is 3 times as large as 18,932 + 921, with no calculating needed.
body_html:
What is a numerical expression?

A numerical expression is numbers and operation signs with no equal sign, like 2 × (8 + 7). To evaluate an expression means to find its value. Everyone must get the same value, so we follow one order.

The order of operations

StepDo thisExample
1Grouping symbols ( ), [ ], { } first, the innermost first2 × (8 + 7) = 2 × 15 = 30
2× and ÷, from left to right24 ÷ 4 × 2 = 6 × 2 = 12
3+ and −, from left to right10 − 4 + 3 = 6 + 3 = 9
Example

Evaluate 5 + 3 × 4.

There are no grouping symbols. Multiply first: 3 × 4 = 12. Then add: 5 + 12 = 17.

Answer: 17 (not 32)

Brackets and braces: work from the inside out

When one group is inside another, parentheses ( ) go inside, brackets [ ] go around them, and braces { } go around the brackets. Start with the innermost group.

Write an expression from words

Find the operation words. If a part must be done first but would not be done first by the order of operations, put it in parentheses.

WordsExpression
the sum of 8 and 78 + 7
the difference of 20 and 420 − 4
the product of 6 and 96 × 9
the quotient of 40 and 540 ÷ 5
subtract 5 from 1212 − 5 (not 5 − 12)
add 8 and 7, then multiply by 22 × (8 + 7)
subtract 5 from the product of 6 and 96 × 9 − 5

Interpret an expression without calculating

You can compare expressions by looking at their structure. 3 × (18,932 + 921) is 3 times as large as 18,932 + 921, because it is 3 groups of that sum. (4,520 − 386) ÷ 2 is half as large as 4,520 − 386.

Example

Which is greater: 7 × (468 + 52) or 7 × (468 + 25)?

Both are 7 groups of a sum, and 468 + 52 is the greater sum.

Answer: 7 × (468 + 52)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
5 + 3 × 4 = 8 × 4 = 32Multiply before you add: 5 + 12 = 17
24 ÷ 4 × 2 = 24 ÷ 8 = 3× and ÷ are on the same level. Go left to right: 6 × 2 = 12
20 − 6 + 4 = 20 − 10 = 10+ and − are on the same level. Go left to right: 14 + 4 = 18
Starting with the brackets, not the parentheses inside themWork from the innermost group outward
“Subtract 5 from 12” written as 5 − 12The number you subtract from comes first: 12 − 5
“Twice the sum of 6 and 4” written as 2 × 6 + 4Put the sum in parentheses: 2 × (6 + 4)

faq.q: What is the order of operations in 5th grade?
faq.a: Work inside parentheses, brackets and braces first, starting with the innermost group. Then multiply and divide from left to right, and then add and subtract from left to right. (Some classes call this PEMDAS; exponents come in Grade 6.)

faq.q: What is the difference between parentheses, brackets and braces?
faq.a: They all mean “do this part first.” Parentheses ( ) go inside, brackets [ ] go around them, and braces { } go around brackets, so you can see which group to start with: {20 − [2 × (3 + 1)]} = 12.

faq.q: Does multiplication always come before division?
faq.a: No. Multiplication and division are on the same level, so you do them in order from left to right: 24 ÷ 4 × 2 = 6 × 2 = 12. Addition and subtraction work the same way: 20 − 6 + 4 = 18.

faq.q: What does it mean to interpret an expression without evaluating it?
faq.a: It means telling what an expression shows without finding its value. For example, 3 × (18,932 + 921) is 3 times as large as 18,932 + 921, because it is 3 groups of that sum.

items.q: Which expression has a value of 30?
items.e: 2 × (8 + 7) = 2 × 15 = 30. Without the parentheses, 2 × 8 + 7 = 23, because you multiply before you add.
(33 − 12) ÷ (2 + 1) = 21 ÷ (2 + 1) = 21 ÷ 3 = 7. Not 28: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
9 × (10 − 6) = 9 × 4 = 36. Without the parentheses the value changes: 9 × 10 − 6 = 84.
(11 + 5) × 8 = 16 × 8 = 128. Not 51: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
(14 − 3) × 4 = 11 × 4 = 44. Not 2: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
(54 + 12) ÷ 6 = 66 ÷ 6 = 11. Not 56: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
(1,600 − 160) ÷ 8 = 1,440 ÷ 8 = 180. Not 1,580: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
(7 + 6) × (9 − 5) = 13 × (9 − 5) = 13 × 4 = 52. Not 56: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
5 + 8 × (11 − 4) = 5 + 8 × 7 = 5 + 56 = 61. Not 89: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
(4 + 3) × 6 − 5 = 7 × 6 − 5 = 42 − 5 = 37. Not 17: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
8 × (10 − 7) = 8 × 3 = 24. Not 73: that comes from skipping the parentheses.

items.q: Which expression has a value of 84?
items.e: 6 × (10 + 4) = 6 × 14 = 84. Without the parentheses, 6 × 10 + 4 = 64, because you multiply before you add.

items.q: Which expression has a value of 48?
items.e: 4 × (9 + 3) = 4 × 12 = 48. Without the parentheses, 4 × 9 + 3 = 39, because you multiply before you add.
59 − (13 + 7) = 59 − 20 = 39. Not 53: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
8 × (12 + 6) = 8 × 18 = 144. Not 102: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
(12 + 5) × 3 = 17 × 3 = 51. Without the parentheses the value changes: 12 + 5 × 3 = 27.

items.q: Which expression has the same value as 6 + (4 × 5)?
items.e: 6 + (4 × 5) = 6 + 20 = 26. 6 + 4 × 5 is also 26, because you multiply first anyway. (6 + 4) × 5 = 50 is different.
80 − (18 − 4) = 80 − 14 = 66. Not 58: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
72 ÷ (12 − 4) = 72 ÷ 8 = 9. Not 2: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
4 × (1,300 + 300) = 4 × 1,600 = 6,400. Not 5,500: that comes from skipping the parentheses.

sets.title: Order of operations: × and ÷ before + and −

items.e: 20 − 6 + 4 = 14 + 4 = 18. Mia added before subtracting, but + and − go from left to right.

items.q: Which part of 40 − 8 + 2 × 5 do you work out first?
items.e: Multiply first: 40 − 8 + 10. Then go left to right: 32 + 10 = 42.

items.q: Which part of 30 ÷ 5 × 2 + 4 do you work out first?
items.e: × and ÷ are on the same level, so go left to right: 30 ÷ 5 = 6 first. Then 6 × 2 = 12, and 12 + 4 = 16.

items.q: Which part of 18 − 6 ÷ 3 + 2 do you work out first?
items.e: Divide first because ÷ comes before + and −: 18 − 2 + 2. Then go left to right: 16 + 2 = 18.
24 ÷ 4 × 2 = 6 × 2 = 12. Grace multiplied before dividing, but × and ÷ go from left to right.
8 × 9 − 6 ÷ 3 = 72 − 6 ÷ 3 = 72 − 2 = 70. Not 22: that comes from working strictly left to right.
7 × 3 + 5 × 4 = 21 + 5 × 4 = 21 + 20 = 41. Not 104: that comes from working strictly left to right.
3 + 6 × 7 = 3 + 42 = 45. Not 63: that comes from working strictly left to right.
8 + 32 ÷ 4 = 8 + 8 = 16. Not 10: that comes from working strictly left to right.
7 × 290 − 31 + 11 = 2,030 − 31 + 11 = 1,999 + 11 = 2,010. Not 1,988: that comes from adding before subtracting.
84 − 48 ÷ 4 × 2 = 84 − 12 × 2 = 84 − 24 = 60. Not 78: that comes from multiplying before dividing.
67 − 20 + 12 = 47 + 12 = 59. Not 35: that comes from adding before subtracting.
6 + 4 × 5 = 6 + 20 = 26. Jack added first, but you multiply before you add.
72 ÷ 4 × 2 = 18 × 2 = 36. Not 9: that comes from multiplying before dividing.
26 − 7 + 3 = 19 + 3 = 22. Not 16: that comes from adding before subtracting.
51 − 15 + 20 − 2 = 36 + 20 − 2 = 56 − 2 = 54. Not 14: that comes from adding before subtracting.
24 − 16 ÷ 4 + 8 = 24 − 4 + 8 = 20 + 8 = 28. Not 10: that comes from working strictly left to right.
126 ÷ 3 × 2 = 42 × 2 = 84. Not 21: that comes from multiplying before dividing.
6 + 7 × 4 − 2 = 6 + 28 − 2 = 34 − 2 = 32. Not 50: that comes from working strictly left to right.
49 − 5 × 4 = 49 − 20 = 29. Not 176: that comes from working strictly left to right.

sets.title: Brackets and braces: work from the inside out

items.e: {[(6 + 5) × 4] − 8} ÷ 2 = {[11 × 4] − 8} ÷ 2 = {44 − 8} ÷ 2 = 36 ÷ 2 = 18. Work from the inside out. Not 9: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
50 × [60 − (23 + 9)] = 50 × [60 − 32] = 50 × 28 = 1,400. Work from the inside out. Not 2,300: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.

items.q: Which part of 6 × [10 − (2 + 5)] do you work out first?
items.e: Start with the innermost grouping symbols, the parentheses: 2 + 5. Then work outward: 6 × [10 − (2 + 5)] = 6 × [10 − 7] = 6 × 3 = 18.
[(12 + 6) ÷ 3] × 2 = [18 ÷ 3] × 2 = 6 × 2 = 12. Sofia skipped the parentheses and divided 6 ÷ 3 first.
[(24 + 8) ÷ 4] × 2 = [32 ÷ 4] × 2 = 8 × 2 = 16. Work from the inside out. Not 52: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
[8 × (7 + 6)] − [5 × (9 − 4)] = [8 × 13] − [5 × (9 − 4)] = 104 − [5 × (9 − 4)] = 104 − [5 × 5] = 104 − 25 = 79. Work from the inside out. Not 21: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
7 × [23 − (14 − 4)] = 7 × [23 − 10] = 7 × 13 = 91. Work from the inside out. Not 35: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
2 × {12 + [32 − (3 × 5)]} = 2 × {12 + [32 − 15]} = 2 × {12 + 17} = 2 × 29 = 58. Work from the inside out. Not 41: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
[31 − (9 + 5)] × 3 = [31 − 14] × 3 = 17 × 3 = 51. Work from the inside out. Not 81: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
[4 + (5 × 3)] × 6 = [4 + 15] × 6 = 19 × 6 = 114. Work from the inside out. Not 94: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
{[7 × (11 − 3)] + 8} ÷ 2 = {[7 × 8] + 8} ÷ 2 = {56 + 8} ÷ 2 = 64 ÷ 2 = 32. Work from the inside out. Not 41: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
[1,300 − (25 × 8)] ÷ 4 = [1,300 − 200] ÷ 4 = 1,100 ÷ 4 = 275. Work from the inside out. Not 1,250: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
60 − [(7 + 4) × 3] = 60 − [11 × 3] = 60 − 33 = 27. Work from the inside out. Not 41: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
16 + [7 × (14 − 4)] = 16 + [7 × 10] = 16 + 70 = 86. Work from the inside out. Not 110: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
{30 − [3 × (2 + 4)]} = {30 − [3 × 6]} = {30 − 18} = 12. Maya skipped the parentheses inside the brackets.

items.q: Which part of [30 − (4 × 5)] ÷ 2 do you work out first?
items.e: Start with the innermost grouping symbols, the parentheses: 4 × 5. Then work outward: [30 − (4 × 5)] ÷ 2 = [30 − 20] ÷ 2 = 10 ÷ 2 = 5.
[3 + (4 × 2)] × 5 = [3 + 8] × 5 = 11 × 5 = 55. Eli skipped the grouping symbols and multiplied first.

items.q: Which part of {20 − [2 × (3 + 1)]} do you work out first?
items.e: Start with the innermost grouping symbols, the parentheses: 3 + 1. Then work outward: {20 − [2 × (3 + 1)]} = {20 − [2 × 4]} = {20 − 8} = 12.
{65 − [3 × (4 + 1)]} = {65 − [3 × 5]} = {65 − 15} = 50. Work from the inside out. Not 54: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
{120 ÷ [2 × (9 − 3)]} + 8 = {120 ÷ [2 × 6]} + 8 = {120 ÷ 12} + 8 = 10 + 8 = 18. Work from the inside out. Not 545: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.

sets.title: Write expressions from words and place parentheses

items.e: The parentheses are worked first: 9 − 2, which is “subtract 2 from 9.” Then the result is multiplied by 4.

items.q:
Where do the parentheses go to make the equation true?
2 × 8 + 10 × 4 = 144

Where do the parentheses go to make the equation true?
3 × 6 − 8 ÷ 2 = 5

Where do the parentheses go to make the equation true?
5 + 8 × 9 + 2 = 119

c: Divide 3 by the sum of 18 and 6
items.e: The parentheses come first: add 18 and 6. Then divide that sum by 3. (18 + 6) ÷ 3 = 24 ÷ 3 = 8.

items.q:
Which expression matches the words?
Subtract 5 from the product of 6 and 9.
items.e: “The product of 6 and 9” is 6 × 9. “Subtract 5 from” it means take 5 away from it: 6 × 9 − 5 = 49. 5 − 6 × 9 has the order backward.

items.q:
Where do the parentheses go to make the equation true?
12 − 5 + 3 × 2 = 20

Which expression matches the words?
Multiply 4 by the sum of 12 and 3.
items.e: “The sum of 12 and 3” is 12 + 3, and it must be found first, so it goes in parentheses: 4 × (12 + 3) = 60.

items.q:
Where do the parentheses go to make the equation true?
9 + 2 × 10 − 4 = 106

Which expression matches the words?
Divide 36 by 4, then subtract the result from 20.
items.e: 36 ÷ 4 is the result. “Subtract the result from 20” means 20 − (36 ÷ 4). Division comes first anyway: 20 − 36 ÷ 4 = 20 − 9 = 11.

items.q:
Which expression matches the words?
The product of 7 and the difference of 20 and 4
items.e: “The difference of 20 and 4” is 20 − 4. Multiply it by 7, so it needs parentheses: 7 × (20 − 4) = 7 × 16 = 112.

items.q:
Which expression matches the words?
Divide the difference of 30 and 6 by 4.
items.e: “The difference of 30 and 6” is 30 − 6. Put it in parentheses so you subtract first, then divide by 4: (30 − 6) ÷ 4 = 6.

items.q:
Where do the parentheses go to make the equation true?
12 − 2 × 3 + 6 = 36

Where do the parentheses go to make the equation true?
11 + 12 ÷ 4 × 3 = 12

Which expression matches the words?
Add 8 and 7, then multiply by 2.
items.e: Add first, so 8 + 7 goes in parentheses. Then multiply by 2: 2 × (8 + 7) = 30. 2 × 8 + 7 would multiply first.

c: Subtract 20 from the product of 3 and 4
Subtract the product of 3 and 4 from 20
items.e: Multiplication comes first, so 3 × 4 is found first. Then it is taken away from 20: 20 − 12 = 8.

items.q:
Which expression matches the words?
Subtract 8 from 50, then divide by 6.
items.e: “Subtract 8 from 50” is 50 − 8, not 8 − 50. It comes first, so it goes in parentheses: (50 − 8) ÷ 6 = 42 ÷ 6 = 7.

items.q:
Which expression matches the words?
Add 9 to the quotient of 40 and 5.
items.e: “The quotient of 40 and 5” is 40 ÷ 5. Add 9 to it: 40 ÷ 5 + 9 = 8 + 9 = 17. No parentheses are needed, because ÷ comes first anyway.

items.q:
Which expression matches the words?
Add the product of 3 and 8 to the product of 5 and 2.
items.e: Each product is a multiplication: 3 × 8 and 5 × 2. Then add them: 3 × 8 + 5 × 2 = 24 + 10 = 34.

items.q:
Which expression matches the words?
Three times the sum of 15 and 6
items.e: “Three times” something means 3 × that amount. The amount is the sum 15 + 6, so it goes in parentheses: 3 × (15 + 6) = 63.

sets.title: Interpret expressions and solve word problems

items.q: Nora says 6 × (250 + 39) is 6 more than 250 + 39. Is she right?
c: No, it is 6 times as large
No, it is 39 times as large
items.e: 6 × (250 + 39) is 6 groups of 250 + 39, so it is 6 times as large. It would be 6 more only if it were 250 + 39 + 6.

items.q: Zoe saves $12 a week for 5 weeks. Then she spends $18. Which expression shows how much money she has now?
items.e: Zoe saves 12 × 5 dollars. Then $18 is taken away: 12 × 5 − 18 = 60 − 18 = 42. 18 − 12 × 5 has the order backward.

items.q: 28 students and 4 teachers split into 2 equal groups for a field trip. Which expression shows how many people are in each group?
items.e: First find everyone: 28 + 4. Then split into 2 groups. The sum must be found first, so it goes in parentheses: (28 + 4) ÷ 2 = 16.

items.q: Without calculating, how does 3 × (18,932 + 921) compare with 18,932 + 921?
items.e: 3 × (18,932 + 921) is 3 groups of the sum 18,932 + 921, so it is 3 times as large. Adding 3 would make it only 3 more.

items.q: Without calculating, how does 8 × 395 + 8 compare with 8 × 395?
items.e: 8 × 395 + 8 is 8 × 395 with 8 added, so it is 8 more. The + 8 is not multiplied, because there are no parentheses.

items.q: Ben buys 3 packs of 12 pencils and 5 extra pencils. Which expression shows how many pencils he buys?
items.e: 3 packs of 12 is 3 × 12. The 5 extra pencils are added once, not to every pack: 3 × 12 + 5 = 36 + 5 = 41.

items.q: Without calculating, how does (4,520 − 386) ÷ 2 compare with 4,520 − 386?
items.e: Dividing by 2 splits the difference 4,520 − 386 into 2 equal parts, so the value is half as large.

items.q: Without calculating, how does 10 × (73 + 1,409) compare with 73 + 1,409?
items.e: 10 × (73 + 1,409) is 10 groups of the sum 73 + 1,409, so it is 10 times as large.
Both are 7 groups of a sum. 468 + 52 is greater than 468 + 25, so 7 × (468 + 52) is greater.

items.q: A movie ticket costs $9 and a bag of popcorn costs $5. A family of 4 gets a ticket and a bag of popcorn for each person. They pay with a $100 bill. How much change do they get?
items.e: Write one expression and evaluate it: 100 − 4 × (9 + 5) = 100 − 4 × 14 = 100 − 56 = 44. Not $69: that skips the parentheses. Not $56: that is the cost, not the change. Answer: $44.

items.q: Which expression is twice as large as 645 + 317?
items.e: Twice as large means 2 groups of the whole sum, so the sum goes in parentheses: 2 × (645 + 317). 2 × 645 + 317 doubles only 645.

items.q: Each of 6 tables has 4 red cups and 5 blue cups. Which expression shows how many cups there are in all?
items.e: Each table has 4 + 5 cups, and there are 6 tables: 6 × (4 + 5) = 6 × 9 = 54. 6 × 4 + 5 forgets the blue cups on 5 of the tables.
Both use the same sum, 2,346 + 78. 5 groups of it are more than 4 groups, so 5 × (2,346 + 78) is greater.
9,000 − (45 + 12) takes away both 45 and 12. 9,000 − 45 + 12 takes away 45 and then adds 12 back, so it is greater.

items.q: Which expression is 4 times as large as 9 × 1,206?
items.e: Multiplying 9 × 1,206 by 4 makes it 4 times as large: 4 × 9 × 1,206. Adding 4 makes it only 4 more.

items.q: Noah has $50. He buys 4 books that cost $9 each. Which expression shows how much money he has left?
items.e: The books cost 4 × 9. Take that away from 50: 50 − 4 × 9 = 50 − 36 = 14. Multiplication comes first, so no parentheses are needed.

items.q: A school orders 12 boxes of 24 markers. 30 markers are broken. The rest are shared equally by 6 classes. How many markers does each class get?
items.e: Write one expression and evaluate it: (12 × 24 − 30) ÷ 6 = (288 − 30) ÷ 6 = 258 ÷ 6 = 43. The subtraction must come before the division, so it goes in parentheses. Not 283: that divides before subtracting. Answer: 43 markers.

items.q: Sam had 120 stickers. He gave 15 stickers to each of 4 friends. Which expression shows how many stickers he has left?
items.e: Sam gave away 4 × 15 stickers. Take that from 120: 120 − 4 × 15 = 120 − 60 = 60.

items.q: A class trip costs $1,250 for each adult and $875 for each child. How much do 3 adults and 2 children pay in all?
items.e: Write one expression and evaluate it: 3 × 1,250 + 2 × 875 = 3,750 + 2 × 875 = 3,750 + 1,750 = 5,500. Multiply each price by the number of people first, then add. Not $4,625: that counts only 1 child. Answer: $5,500.

items.q: A bakery makes 8 trays of 15 muffins and 4 trays of 12 muffins. At the end of the day, 20 muffins are left. How many muffins did the bakery sell?
items.e: Write one expression and evaluate it: 8 × 15 + 4 × 12 − 20 = 120 + 4 × 12 − 20 = 120 + 48 − 20 = 168 − 20 = 148. Find both products first and add them, then subtract the 20 muffins that were left. 168 is all the muffins, not the ones sold. Answer: 148 muffins.
